articles.title: The Quiet Collapse of the Senate's Middle Ground
articles.excerpt: For decades, the Senate prided itself on its moderates — the dealmakers who kept the institution from breaking. They are nearly gone now, and Washington is only beginning to reckon with what that means.

articles.title: Inside the White House Communications War
articles.excerpt: Two factions, one message. How competing communications strategies inside the West Wing have left the administration speaking with two very different voices.

articles.title: How the Budget Deal Fell Apart — Again
articles.excerpt: A bipartisan framework was within reach. Then came the weekend. A reconstruction of the 72 hours that killed it.

articles.title: The Lobbyists Who Shaped the Climate Bill
articles.excerpt: Long before the cameras arrived for the signing ceremony, a handful of industry lobbyists had already written the key provisions. A follow-the-money investigation.

articles.title: What the Midterms Really Told Us About American Politics
articles.excerpt: Strip away the horse-race coverage and a more disturbing story emerges — one about structural shifts in how Americans relate to political power.
